user_text: A registry review at an orthopedic group shows their cementless total-knee femoral components revisions for aseptic loosening running at 3.1 percent at 10 years versus the 1.5-percent benchmark, with retrieval analysis of nine revised components showing a fibrous tissue interface instead of bone ingrowth across the anterior flange, where intra-operative measurements suggest micromotion of 80 to 150 microns under stair-climbing load against the widely cited 50-to-75-micron threshold for reliable ingrowth. The implant is a cobalt-chrome femoral component with a 1-millimetre porous coating on the pegs only, and the group's patient mix skews 20 percent heavier than the design cohort. The group must keep the same implant system (surgeon training and hospital contracts lock the platform for 3 more years), cannot change the stem or peg geometry (regulatory changes to the component would re-open the 510(k)), cannot add operative time beyond 5 minutes per case (the block schedule is fixed), and must bring 10-year aseptic loosening at or below 2 percent within the existing surgical workflow.
